div.l: In suche case of þe Archedekenes cours
But if mannys soule were in his purs
For in his porse shuld he punyshed be
The purse is þe Archedekenes hell qd he
But wel I wote he leide in dede
Of cursing ought eche man haue drede
For cursing sleeth right as a soiling saueth
And also be ware him of a significauit
In danger had he at his owne gise
The yong girles of þe diocise
And knew her counseill and was her rede
A garland had he vpon his hede
As grete as it were for an ale stake
A bokeler had he made him of a kake
With him þere rode a gentil ꝑpardoner
Of rowncivale his frende and his cōmper
That streite was come fro þe courte of rome
Ful loude he sange come hither loue Thome
This sompnour bare with him a stif burdon̄
Was neuer troumpe of half so grete a sown̄
This ꝑpardoner had her as yelowe as flex
Smothe it was and hang as flax
Be vnces hang his lokkes þat he hadde
And þere with he . his shulders ouer spradde
But thin it lay be culpons oon and one
But hode for iolite wered he none
For it was trussed vp in his valet
Him þought he rode al of þe nowe iet
Discheuele safe his cappe . he rode al bare
Suche glaring eien̄ hadde he as an hare
A vernace hadde he sewed on his cappe
His valet befor him in his lappe
Bratful of pardoıı̄un that came from Rome al hote
A voice he had assmale as hath a gote
No berde hadde nor neuer shal haue
Assmoth it was as it were newe shaue
I trow he were a gilding or a mare
But of his craft from berwik vnto ware
Ne was þer suche a ꝑpardoner
For in his male he had a pilewe ber
Which he seid was ouer leide wele
He seid eke he had a gobet of þe sele
That seint petre had whan that he went
